from: October book, night 5 (I Called You by Name)
p1: Isaiah wrote the Lord’s words for His people. Hard times would come, and they might feel all alone.
The Lord said, “Fear not. I have called you by your name. You are Mine.” He knows each person, and He loves them.
The Lord said, “When you pass through the waters, I will be with you. The rivers will not cover you.”
p2: Crossing a deep river can feel scary. So Isaiah used the river as a picture of hard times. The Lord who spoke was Jesus. He promised to be with them in every hard time.
Jesus knows your name too. Tonight, say softly, “I am His, and He loves me.”
old: Long ago, Heavenly Father's people had to leave their homes and live far away in a land called Babylon. They missed home. The walk back would be long and hard, and Heavenly Father told them the truth about that. He did not say it would be easy.

He said something better. A prophet named Isaiah carried the words: "Do not be afraid. I made you. I called you by your name. You are Mine." Being called by name means Heavenly Father knows exactly who you are — not a crowd, you.

"When you walk through deep water, I will be with you. The river will not wash you away." Deep water was a picture for the scary parts of the trip. The people remembered Moses, when Heavenly Father made a dry path through the Red Sea. Heavenly Father was saying, I did that for you before. I will be with you again.

"When you walk through fire, you will not be burned. I am your Savior." Fire was a picture for the hottest, hardest days. A Savior is someone who saves you. Isaiah was talking about Jesus. Jesus is our Savior.
Heavenly Father did not promise there would be no deep water. He promised something better: He would be right there in it with them. Beau found that out at the pool, holding tight to the wall.
